# 1.2.28 - the audit of 1.2.27, carried out

The identity audit was re-run against the module as it shipped in 1.2.27,
with one screenshot from a tablet and a reading of every rule the theme
writes. This release is that audit's list, in the order the audit said to
work it: the faces first, because until the pixel sweep stopped winning
nothing else could be judged on screen; then the signals the glass is cut
from; then everything the two of them were hiding.

## The faces

**The pixel face belongs to Monokuma Legacy.** "Pixel font" was a *world*
setting, on by default, and the two `!important` sweeps it switches on
outrank 27 of the 30 font rules in the theme's own sheet. A table on the
defaults therefore saw Press Start 2P under **both** themes: Stained Glass
never showed VT323 or Special Elite unless a GM took the pixel face away from
everyone still on Legacy. It is a client setting now, read only under Legacy -
which keeps Press Start 2P as its default face, with nothing to turn on - and
the switch lives in the Look window, where it is shown to the browsers it
still means something to.

Nine synthesised bolds and one italic are set back to 400 and normal: neither
VT323 nor Special Elite has a bold or an italic, so the browser was faking
them by smearing the glyphs. The title face loses the one letter-spacing it
had left. The 11 px floor is a token instead of a comment, and
`docs/design/typography.md` is the page these rules were only ever written on.

Eleven surfaces that still spoke Signika, Bahnschrift or the pixel face beside
a window speaking VT323 now speak the theme: the GM bar, the camera dock, the
latency and frame counter, the messenger's note and roster, an item sheet's
prose, the roll card's headings, the overflow caption, the check report,
Foundry's tooltip where it lands inside our windows, and a stray label and
button on the character sheet. Foundry's own configuration windows are
deliberately left alone.

## The glass knows what the screen is doing

**The wall.** An expanded sidebar cuts the glass short, and whether it was
expanded was decided by measuring it - so the one rebuild the collapse hook
scheduled ran while Foundry was still animating the panel shut, read 300 px of
sidebar, and left the wall at 1685 px with the right-hand column standing
outside the glass. Foundry is asked instead. The blocks' rectangles are part
of the signature, so a block that moves without changing size recuts the
glass; a drift watch samples them twice a second for the cases no observer
sees, and recuts only once a layout has read the same twice in a row.

**The tilt.** The slope field and the upright zone in the middle were read off
the wall rather than the screen, which is why the Despair rail leaned on the
screenshot. Below 2200 px the blocks stand straight: at 8 degrees a tablet
reads the clock's two faces across a third of the screen.

**The notice pane** was cut for `#drpg-notice`, an element no script has ever
built. It measures `#drpg-popups`, with no fallback, and the notices move onto
it - bottom-left, where the audit page draws them.

## What was under the black plates

Every pane tone went up a step, and the black layer over a panel's pane is
half weight. At #050409 under 68 % alpha with 30 % black over it, a pane over
a dark map is not dark glass; it is a black rectangle with writing on it. The
tray's pane is the size of the tray (a 150 px floor bought corner balance with
a black slab carrying one line), and the shard cut for Foundry's tiles is kept
plain black only when tiles actually sit on it.

## Nothing in the chrome is cut off

"MONOKUMA" read as "MUNUKUMA" on the screenshot, and the same on "AFTERNOON"
and "STILL TO ACT". The correction shipped in 1.2.26 - written under
`body.drpg-pixel-font`, so the face that needed it never got it. It is the
chrome's rule now: a line box of 1.35, no `overflow: hidden` on a box that
only holds a label, an ellipsis kept for names a person typed. The hour's
chevrons sit 8 px off the word instead of 30, the Despair rows are columns
that line up with each other, and chapter and day are one line.

## Five families the audit found missing

The phase on the clock is a stamp with the hour's pixel glyph on it. Every
Event card carries the glyph of what it is. A popup's title band is Bone, with
the kind speaking through the seam. The Despair pips take the theme's colour
and the steppers take the brush. The checkbox is a square with the sprite's
tick cut out of it.

## The interface scale, and the cost of a turn

`zoom` on `#interface` scaled the wrong half of the interface - windows,
dialogs, popups and the curtain all live on `document.body` - and left Foundry
remembering window positions in pixels they were never drawn in. The scale is
a factor on the theme's own type and block sizes, floored at 11 px.

The turn's transitions are a named list instead of every descendant of every
module element; `will-change` is held only while something turns; and folding
the Projects tray no longer swaps the whole curtain for the morph canvas for
840 ms - the morph runs when the screen changes state or when the shape really
did change.

## Three tests

The curtain's self-check has to come back clean, no chrome label may be taller
than its box, and nothing in the chrome may be set under the floor. All three
are things no reading of the code could have caught.
